● I wrote docs/how-it-works.md, added its line to docs/INDEX.md, and committed both as 713dff9 "docs: how it works" on trace. Nothing else was staged, and I didn't push. The # REPORT is
  appended to handoffs/reports/howto.md; I left that file uncommitted because the brief only says to append.

  What I measured (read-only, 15:32–15:40 IST, about 2.5 minutes after a restart):
  - Speed: a fast-path reply starts speaking about 2.35 s (median) after the mic decides you've stopped. A Claude reply takes about 5.3 s (median, range 3.1–9.1). Speech-to-text takes
    about 0.4 s either way. This comes from 29 voice turns in the journal, matched to brain.log.
  - Local models: speech-to-text (whisper large-v3-turbo) and the voice (Kokoro, af_heart) run on the GPU. Voice detection runs on the CPU. The wake word and speaker check are both off.
    Model files take 2.3 GB on disk.
  - Claude: this is the only part that isn't local. It runs on your subscription (apiKeySource: none, Haiku). Cost per turn shows as $0.0001–$0.0014, but that's what Claude Code reports
    as the API equivalent, not a charge. It counts against your plan's usage limits.
  - GPU while idle: 2850 MiB of video memory held, 0% load, 3.3 W in its lowest power state. heardbackd uses 2.9 GiB of RAM and 0–1% CPU. I didn't measure GPU load during a turn, because
    the brief said not to trigger turns or play audio.

  Things in the code that surprised me (all in the report):
  1. The live service runs your working copy, not the installed snapshot. heardback.service uses uv run --project on the repo, and Claude's jv tools come from the repo's .venv too. So
     whichever branch is checked out at restart is what runs. The 15:29 restart is running the trace branch right now. The handoff's "worker edits never reach live" is only true for the
     hooks.
  2. The stt_model setting in voice.toml does nothing. The code checks it but always loads the same model.
  3. Fast-path replies aren't instant, and the timer may overstate them. About 1.5 s of the ~2 s is unaccounted for, probably voice synthesis plus starting the audio player. The "first
     audio" time is recorded only after the first sentence is fully handed to the player, so long first sentences probably look slower than they are.
  4. The 15:15 refusal to type into tmux was a bug, not a refusal. brain.log's denied … reason='active' was a KeyError: 'active' inside the tmux command, which is what trace task 6 is
     fixing.
